label: input p right after e, early in a sequence starting with t (t-..-e-p)
explanation: Very sparse: 65 activations on 65 of 1M sequences. Nearly all of the activation mass is at original-phase steps 3-5 where the input is p, the previous input is e, and the sequence starts with t (as in t v e e [p], t y u e [p], t u e [p]). It never fires at t<3, and never in the copy phase except for one weak delimiter case. A few weak activations fit only part of the pattern: a non-p input after a t...u e prefix (o, 0, <DEL>), p after o or 2, or a sequence starting with p or 2. The predicate is imprecise (dev precision about 0.29): many t..e p sequences at the same steps stay silent, and the profile does not show what separates them. Strongest activations come when the prefix has a u, v or y before the e, but there are too few examples to check this as a magnitude claim.
